questions.question: What is modulation?
questions.tutor: Modulation varies carrier properties (amplitude, frequency, phase) with message signal.

questions.question: What is AM?
questions.tutor: AM varies carrier amplitude according to message signal.

questions.question: What is FM?
questions.tutor: FM varies carrier frequency according to message signal.

questions.question: What is PM?
questions.tutor: PM varies carrier phase according to message signal.

questions.question: What is the advantage of FM over AM?
questions.tutor: FM is more immune to amplitude noise because information is in frequency.

questions.question: What is bandwidth?
questions.tutor: Bandwidth is the difference between highest and lowest frequencies in a signal.

questions.question: What is the Nyquist theorem?
questions.tutor: Nyquist: sampling rate must be at least twice the highest frequency to avoid aliasing.

questions.question: What is aliasing?
questions.tutor: Aliasing occurs when sampling rate is below Nyquist, causing high frequencies to appear as low.

questions.question: What is PCM?
questions.tutor: PCM converts analog signal to digital by sampling, quantizing, and encoding.

questions.question: What is a transceiver?
questions.tutor: Transceiver combines transmitter and receiver in one unit.

questions.question: What is a duplex communication?
questions.tutor: Duplex allows both parties to transmit and receive simultaneously (full-duplex).

questions.question: What is simplex communication?
questions.tutor: Simplex is one-way (e.g., radio broadcast).

questions.question: What is multiplexing?
choices: Combining multiple signals on one channel
questions.tutor: Multiplexing shares a single channel among multiple users or signals.

questions.question: What is TDM?
questions.tutor: TDM allocates time slots to different signals on same channel.

questions.question: What is FDM?
questions.tutor: FDM assigns different frequency bands to different signals.

questions.question: What is a modem?
questions.tutor: Modem converts digital data to analog for transmission and back.

questions.question: What is the Shannon-Hartley theorem?
questions.tutor: Shannon gives maximum channel capacity (bps) for given bandwidth and SNR.

questions.question: What is a decibel (dB)?
questions.tutor: dB = 10 log₁₀(P1/P2) for power ratio.

questions.question: What is dBm?
questions.tutor: dBm is power relative to 1 milliwatt (0 dBm = 1 mW).

questions.question: What is a filter?
questions.tutor: Filter allows desired frequencies to pass while attenuating others.

questions.question: What is a low-pass filter?
questions.tutor: Low-pass filter attenuates frequencies above cutoff frequency.

questions.question: What is a high-pass filter?
questions.tutor: High-pass filter attenuates frequencies below cutoff frequency.

questions.question: What is a band-pass filter?
questions.tutor: Band-pass filter passes frequencies between lower and upper cutoffs.

questions.question: What is the electromagnetic spectrum order from low to high frequency?
choices: Radio, Microwave, Infrared, Visible, UV, X-ray, Gamma
Gamma, X-ray, UV, Visible, IR, Microwave, Radio
questions.tutor: Frequency increases from radio waves to gamma rays.

questions.question: What is the typical frequency range for FM radio broadcast?
questions.tutor: FM radio occupies 88 to 108 MHz band.
